issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings of guilt should not be disturbed when the evidence supports the prosecution case and the circumstances raised by the defence do not undermine it.
material_facts: The lower courts accepted the prosecution’s account, relying on witness testimony and the deceased’s dying declaration.
The defence relied on the prior dispute, the location and trails of blood, weapons found at the scene, bone fragments, blood marks on walls, and the accused’s account of the incident.

The Court found the prior dispute neutral; the proposed blood trails were unsupported by evidence; blood in the dalan did not establish that the fight began there; the weapons could fit the prosecution case; the bone fragments were not shown to be human; and the source of the blood marks was not proved.
The accused’s account did not explain the injuries to the deceased and witnesses.
The challenged account of the deceased being “dragged” was understood as meaning that he was caught and forcibly taken into the dalan.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances raised by the defence did not justify disturbing the concurrent findings of guilt. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court ordinarily does not interfere with concurrent factual findings. A prior dispute may be neutral, and scene evidence that is unsupported, ambiguous, or equally consistent with the prosecution case does not by itself displace accepted oral evidence and a dying declaration. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_concurrent_f: The accused brought a criminal appeal challenging concurrent findings of guilt by the lower courts.
predicates.prosecution_testimony_and_dying_declarat: The lower courts relied on witness testimony and the deceased’s dying declaration to support the prosecution account.
predicates.defence_scene_evidence_was_ambiguous_or_: The defence relied on scene circumstances whose significance for its account was unsupported, ambiguous, or also consistent with the prosecution account.
predicates.accused_account_did_not_explain_the_inju: The accused gave an account that did not explain the injuries sustained by the deceased and witnesses.

issues.definition: When an accused challenges concurrent findings in a criminal appeal, and the prosecution evidence supports its case while the defence scene evidence is ambiguous or unsubstantiated and the accused’s account leaves the injuries unexplained, the findings are left undisturbed.
